messages.subject: Epidemiological epicurve
parts:
Dear list members I have the dataset  and I want to construct the epicurve similar to this. 

This is the code I used
>flu <- read.csv("C:/Users/symon/Desktop/flu epicurve.csv")
> require(date)
 # Format the date
> flu$Date_epi <- strptime(flu$Date_epi, format= "%d/%m/%Y")
>format(flu$Date_epi, format="%Y-%m-%d")
> str(flu)
# plot the epicurve
> hist(flu$Date_epi[(flu$Sex=="F")], "weeks", 
    format = "%d %b %Y", freq=T, col=rgb(0,0,0,1), axes=F, main="")
> hist(flu$Date_epi[(flu$Sex=="M")], "weeks", 
     format = "%d %b %y", freq=T, col=rgb(0,0,0,1), axes=F, main="")
> axis.Date(1, at=seq(as.Date("2014-06-03"), as.Date("2014-07-19"), by="1 week"), format="%d %b %y")
> axis.Date(1, at=seq(as.Date("2014-06-03"), as.Date("2014-07-19"), by="weeks"), 
          labels=F, tcl= -0.5)
But this is what I obtain(two different graph) than what I expected) could anyone help me plot the epicurve similar to the above
​​

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Epidemiological epicurve
parts:
What about something like this?

flu$Date_epi <- strptime(flu$Date_epi, format= "%Y-%m-%d")

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(flu, aes(x = Date_epi, fill = Classification)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_histogram(position = "dodge")

I don't know which variable you want to use to group the data, I chose Classification.

Cheers,
Roman
